claims.text: Rapidly quenched FeCoNiTi has a dual-phase microstructure consisting of an fcc matrix and hexagonal C14 Laves-phase precipitates.
The fcc matrix in the dual-phase FeCoNiTi alloy is ferromagnetic.
The C14 phase contains a Ti-rich sublattice.
The Ti-rich C14 sublattice couples antiferromagnetically to Fe, Co, and Ni moments in the adjacent fcc matrix.
Antiferromagnetic coupling across the fcc/C14 interface locally reduces the net magnetic moment and saturation magnetization of the fcc phase.
The fcc/C14 phase boundaries are strong domain-wall pinning sites.
The distinct magnetic anisotropy of the C14 phase contributes to domain-wall pinning.
Crystallographic mismatch between the fcc and C14 phases creates a high-energy barrier to domain-wall motion.
Phase separation can reduce saturation magnetization and increase coercivity in a high-entropy alloy.
The combined antiferromagnetic coupling and interfacial pinning mechanisms overcome an intrinsic coercivity limit of approximately 100 Oe in single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni alloys.
The approximately 100 Oe coercivity limit of single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni alloys arises from insufficient orbital moments.
The dual-phase FeCoNiTi alloy will exhibit a coercivity of approximately 667 Oe at 400 K.
Saturation magnetization will decrease in proportion to the C14 phase fraction.
Controlled annealing can systematically vary the C14 volume fraction and fcc/C14 interfacial density while maintaining the bulk fcc composition.
The proposed pinning mechanism requires the C14 phase to remain structurally intact and magnetically distinct at 400 K.
Spin-polarized DFT comparing a bulk fcc model with an explicit fcc/C14 interface model can test changes in spin-resolved density of states at the Fermi level and the interfacial exchange energy.
A comparison between dual-phase and single-phase FeCoNiTi specimens over 300–500 K can test whether C14 formation enhances coercivity and suppresses saturation magnetization.
The hypothesis is falsified if the dual-phase specimen does not exceed 150 Oe at 400 K or if interface DFT finds neither a meaningful spin-DOS change nor antiferromagnetic interfacial exchange.

contradictions.description: Rapid quenching is stated to produce the initial dual-phase fcc/C14 alloy, but it is also proposed as a way to suppress C14 formation and produce the single-phase fcc control, without specifying different quench rates or other conditions that would reconcile the two statements.
